statement: Most acute infectious conjunctivitis is self-limiting; watery discharge and preauricular node suggest viral etiology.
citation: AAO PPP Conjunctivitis [author to verify section/year]

statement: Severe pain, photophobia, or reduced vision are NOT typical of simple conjunctivitis and warrant urgent evaluation for keratitis, uveitis, or angle-closure.
citation: AAO PPP Conjunctivitis — red flags [author to verify]

statement: Anterior uveitis presents with pain, photophobia, and circumlimbal (ciliary) injection; it requires prompt ophthalmologic evaluation and is sight-threatening if untreated.
citation: AAO PPP Uveitis [author to verify section/year]

statement: Vision loss, hypopyon, or markedly elevated IOP with uveitis indicate an emergent, sight-threatening presentation.
citation: AAO PPP Uveitis — red flags [author to verify]

statement: Common eyelid conditions (e.g., hordeolum, chalazion, blepharitis) are usually managed conservatively with warm compresses and lid hygiene.
citation: AAO PPP Blepharitis [author to verify section/year]

statement: Rapidly progressive lid swelling with fever, proptosis, pain on eye movement, or restricted motility suggests orbital cellulitis — an emergency.
citation: AAO guidance on orbital cellulitis [author to verify]

statement: A normal-appearing external eye does not exclude posterior segment or neuro-ophthalmic pathology if symptoms persist.
Isolated subconjunctival hemorrhage is typically benign and self-limiting in the absence of trauma or bleeding disorder.
citation: [author to write and verify — e.g., AAO subconjunctival hemorrhage guidance]

statement: Hemorrhage with pain, vision change, history of trauma, or anticoagulation warrants urgent evaluation to exclude globe rupture or other serious injury.
Any acute vision loss, new floaters/flashes, diplopia, or severe pain requires urgent ophthalmology involvement regardless of external appearance.
citation: AAO general urgent-referral guidance [author to verify]
